sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.1 'The sound system' (pp. 8-9) gives a consonant chart (p, t, ch, k, b, d, j, q, v, s, gh, m, n, ng, l, r), a five-vowel chart and English-comparison pronunciation notes; sec. 3.2 covers alphabet problems. No mention of stress, accent, vowel length or prosody anywhere in the 50-page scan (full-text grep of the scanned layer). Describes the Ghaimuta dialect (Glottolog ghai1237) from one week's fieldwork in Lame village, Nov. 1977.
Nothing on stress; reports 6 vowels (Unger 2008: 5) and 15 consonants with prenasalized voiced stops (Unger 2008: 4), plus pronoun and verb-phrase material; second-hand and silent on accent.
